subject: Geo segmentation: pricing for separate reserved pools + DR options
messages:

Subject: Geo segmentation: pricing for separate reserved pools + DR options

Hi Anita / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation you want a multi-region Dedicated setup with isolated GPU pools in each geography (US East, EU West, AP South) and an SLA that covers both throughput guarantees and a defined failover behavior. To move the commercial conversation forward I sketched two high-level options and attached an initial capacity estimate (region_capacity_estimate.xlsx):

Option A — Separate reserved pools per region (recommended):
- Each region has a dedicated commit (locked capacity) sized to baseline throughput.
- Cross-region routing only on failover (DNS + health checks).
- Strong data residency: EU traffic stays in EU pool.

Option B — Active-active replication with cross-region routing:
- Pools in each region with active replication of models/weights/KV where allowed.
- Higher cost (storage + replication + inter-region egress).

Questions I have for you to finalize numbers:
1) Which regions do you want now vs. later? (You mentioned US & EU first on the call.)
2) Target steady-state concurrency / requests-per-second per region (or tokens/sec) we should size for?
3) RTO/RPO targets for DR (how fast do you need failover; is 60s acceptable?)
4) Will you commit 12 months or 36 months? Longer commits get bigger discounts.

Ballpark pricing in the attached sheet assumes A100-class GPUs and a 12-month commit. If you can share target qps and desired percent headroom (e.g., 20% peak buffer), we’ll convert this into committed vGPU counts and a formal quote.

Next steps: if you’re ok, I’ll loop Dev on sizing and Lauren on commercial terms and we’ll return a formal quote + SOW.

Thanks,
Rafael

Thanks Rafael — good recap. A few clarifications from our side so your sizing is accurate:

1) Regions: we want US East (primary), EU West (data residency for EU customers), and AP South (pilot for APAC customers). We expect to launch EU in Q4.
2) Throughput: baseline steady-state is ~120 inference requests/sec across the fleet, split approx 60% US / 30% EU / 10% APAC. Each request averages ~750 tokens in + 750 tokens out. Plan for 25% headroom for diurnal spikes.
3) DR: target RTO 2 minutes for automatic failover to alternate region; however we are open to an SLA-backed failover plan if that reduces cost.
4) Commit: procurement prefers a 12-month commit initially. We may expand to 24 months after proving latency/cost.

Two important constraints: EU customer data must remain in EU region unless explicitly routed by EU user consent; any active-active replication must be configurable to exclude user payload for EU-resident models. Also procurement will want a credit clause if failover results in >5 minutes increased latency or sustained errors.

I attached a draft SOW with our compliance checklist (GreenFleet_SOW_draft_v2.pdf). Can your team provide a clear delta between Option A and Option B in both $/month and expected failure behavior?

-Anita

Rafael — quick technical breakdown attached and summarized below. I used the request and token averages Anita provided. Assumptions: H100-class perf per GPU, optimized kernel paths, continuous batching.

Sizing (baseline + 25% headroom):
- US East (60% of load): ~72 req/s -> estimate 6x H100 GPUs (packed inference nodes) to hit target with <150ms p50 latency for their model family
- EU West (30%): ~36 req/s -> estimate 3x H100 GPUs
- AP South (10%): ~12 req/s -> estimate 1x H100 GPU (pilot)

Option A — Separate pools (lower net cost / simpler ops):
- Requires separate committed capacity in each region; no inter-region egress for inference traffic.
- Cost drivers: committed GPU hours in each region + minimal synchronization of model artifacts (once per model push).
- Failover: DNS-based active-passive failover; RTO can be ~60–120s depending on cache warmup.

Option B — Active-active replication (higher availability, higher cost):
- Keeps models and KV caches warm in multiple regions; reduces failover RTO to <30s but incurs continuous replication and higher egress/storage costs.
- Requires explicit configuration to avoid replicating EU user payloads (we can replicate models/artifacts but mask or avoid per-user KV syncing).

Cost delta (rough): Option B is ~25–35% more expensive than Option A for continuous active-active. Major extra costs: inter-region egress, storage replication, double-warmed GPU capacity.

Recommendation: Start with Option A (separate committed pools) with a warmed cold-standby in the secondary region for EU/US failover. If they later require sub-30s RTO, move to active-active for the critical subset of traffic.

I attached an updated region_capacity_estimate.xlsx with vGPU counts and an estimated monthly committed price per region at list rates.

-Dev

Thanks all — I pulled Dev’s sizing into commercial terms below. Rafael, please send this back to GreenFleet and let them know we can discuss the final SOW items on a call.

Commercial summary (12-month commit, H100-equivalent capacity):
- US East: committed 6 vGPU-equivalents — list $68,000/month
- EU West: committed 3 vGPU-equivalents — list $34,000/month
- AP South: committed 1 vGPU-equivalent — list $12,000/month
- Total list: $114,000/month

Discounting (multi-region commit):
- Single-region 12mo: up to 10% off list
- Two-region 12mo commit: 15% off combined list
- Three-region 12mo commit: 20% off combined list
- Active-active replication add-on (where we keep warmed capacity and continuous replication): +25% on top of committed cost for the regions participating in active-active.

Failover credits and SLA:
- Standard SLA covers availability and latency (we’ll include regional p50/p95 latency targets in the SOW).
- For failover events causing customer-impacting errors >5 minutes, we can offer a pro-rated service credit (0.5% of monthly committed spend per incident, capped at 5%/month).

Notes & conditions:
- EU data residency: replica behavior must be defined in SOW; we will not replicate user payloads to EU-non-resident regions without explicit consent.
- Egress and cross-region traffic costs are not included in list prices and will be billed at cost if cross-region replication is enabled.

Next steps:
1) Rafael: confirm with GreenFleet acceptance of the 3-region structure and whether they want Option A vs Option B for the pilot phase.
2) If they accept three-region commit at 20% discount, I’ll prepare the formal SOW + DocuSign link.

Rafael — I can authorize up to 20% discount for a three-region, 12-month commit. Anything deeper than that requires approval from Sales Ops.

Thanks,

Lauren / Rafael — appreciate the fast turnaround. A few responses from procurement and product: 

1) Discounting: GreenFleet is willing to commit to a 12-month three-region deal if we can move the discount to 23% (they are a mid-market customer with growth potential). If Sales Ops needs more detail we can share forecasted monthly spend.

2) Failover credits: procurement wants stronger language — propose 1% monthly credit per incident >5 minutes up to 10%/month cap. We understand limits but want remediation that protects our SLA.

3) Active-active: for now we prefer Option A for cost reasons but would like to revisit active-active for EU/US subset after Q4 launch.

If you can update the SOW with the revised credit language and a 23% discount option for a three-region 12-month commit, procurement will expedite internal approvals and return a signed PO. We are ready to bring in our legal team for a short review next week.

-Anita
